sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: owner-scoped lookups and manager direct-report queries; status: lifecycle filtering (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/CANCELLED); leave_type_code, start_date: findByQuery date-range/type filters

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end (unique): findByKey at-most-one-row-per-period invariant; employee_id: employee-scoped balance lookups

table audit_logs | fields: id, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, before_state, after_state, occurred_at | pk: id | fks: actor_id -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit-trail lookup for a given entity; actor_id: actor-scoped audit history

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: recipient inbox lookups; status: pending-notification queue scans

data_notes: No new tables are required: the cancellation flow reuses the existing leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs, and notifications tables (all already defined in prior phases). The leave_requests table already carries the CANCELLED status value (LeaveStatus enum) and the repository's update() already supports status transitions via FIELD_COLUMNS. The balance release is a delta on leave_balances (pendingDays for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, usedDays for APPROVED) via the existing IBalanceRepository.update. Audit and notification reuse the existing audit_logs/notifications tables. No schema changes are needed; the code agent should not generate new migrations for this feature.

open_questions.question: The AuditAction enum (src/shared/types) has CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/APPROVE/REJECT but no CANCEL. The cancel operation must record an audit entry (GP-002); which action value should it use?
open_questions.impact: Determines the persisted audit action for every cancellation and whether the shared enum gains a new member (a cross-module contract change). Affects audit-trail querying/filtering by action.
candidate_options: Add CANCEL = 'CANCEL' to AuditAction and use it for cancellations
Reuse UPDATE for cancellations (no enum change)
Reuse DELETE for cancellations (no enum change)

transaction_contract: Cancellation is a multi-step write (status change + balance release + audit entry + notification) and MUST be atomic. The service owns the unit of work via IUnitOfWork.withTransaction (PgUnitOfWork: acquire a PoolClient from the shared pool, BEGIN, run the callback, COMMIT on success / ROLLBACK on throw, always release). Every repository/service method that must join the caller's transaction takes an OPTIONAL trailing PoolClient parameter and falls back to the shared pool when omitted. The cancel service passes the transaction's client to: ILeaveRepository.update (status -> CANCELLED), IBalanceRepository.update (release pendingDays for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, or usedDays for APPROVED), IAuditService.record, and INotificationService.create. Balance reads that precede a balance write must use findByKey with forUpdate=true (row lock) to avoid lost updates on concurrent decisions.
